hints: Suppose a helper has already reversed everything after the first node. Where does the first node need to go now, and what does it point to?
Recursion on the rest of the list: reverse head.next recursively, then hook head onto the end of that reversed part. The node after head is now the tail, so head.next.next = head.

1. If head is null or has no next node, return it (already reversed).
  2. Let newHead = reverse(head.next).
  3. Set head.next.next = head so the old second node points back to head.
  4. Set head.next = null because head is now the last node.
  5. Return newHead.

approaches.name: Copy into an array
approaches.idea: Store the values, then rebuild or overwrite in reverse order.

approaches.name: Recursive (this problem)
approaches.idea: Reverse the tail, then attach the head at the end.

approaches.name: Iterative three pointers
approaches.idea: Walk with prev/cur/next and flip each link. Same time, O(1) space.

explain: For 7→3→9→1 the call chain goes down to node 1, which is returned as the new head. Back at node 9, we set 1.next = 9 and 9.next = null, giving 1→9. Then at 3 we get 1→9→3, and at 7 we get 1→9→3→7. Forgetting head.next = null leaves a cycle between the first two nodes. An empty list returns null immediately.
recognize: A linked-list problem where 'the rest of the list' is a smaller copy of the same problem → recurse on head.next and fix up the head.
javascript: function reverseList(head) { let p = null; while (head) { const n = head.next; head.next = p; p = head; head = n; } return p; }
